title: Why does swapping not change negative nine plus four?
description: Negative nine plus four is checked against four plus negative nine, using positive and negative counters. Keeko doubts the swap and thinks the order changes how many counters cancel.
teaching_notes: One idea: counters do not change when they are moved, so swapping two terms cannot change the sum. Watch for children who think the order changes how many cancel.

source: Take some more expressions and check whether swapping the terms changes the sum. Can you explain why this is happening using the counters model of integers?
video_script.why: The child explains why swapping two terms keeps the sum, using positive and negative counters.
video_script.substitution: Picture each term as a pile of counters, cancel the pairs, and see that the pile is the same in either order.
video_script.anchor: Nine negative counters and four positive counters
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks that adding the positive counters first would change how many pairs cancel, and so change the sum.

final_answer.spoken: negative nine plus four is negative five, and four plus negative nine is negative five

never_show: a different value for the swapped order
maths_rules: (−9) + 4: nine negative counters and four positive counters
four pairs cancel, so five negative counters are left, and the value is −5
4 + (−9) uses the same counters, so the value is −5
moving counters does not change them
video_script.design: One idea: the same counters give the same sum in either order. Assumes positive and negative counters cancel in pairs. Wrong idea: the order changes how many cancel. The counters stay on the board all video.
